result.title: STARE: Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects
result.summary: In this study, we focus on service robots that retrieve and transport everyday objects based on free-form instructions that may refer to visual features and scene text. This is challenging because it requires a multimodal understanding of the visual features and spatial relationships of objects, as well as scene text embedded in the environment. To address this, we propose Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects (STARE), which leverages visual and textual cues in response to free-form instructions. STARE introduces Crosslingual Visual Prompt to enhance scene text interpretation, and models the complex relationships between named entities in the instructions and their corresponding objects. We evaluate STARE using two novel benchmarks, GoGetIt and TextCaps-test, both of which consist of real-world indoor/outdoor images and instructions involving object manipulation and navigation. The results show that STARE outperforms all baseline methods on standard multimodal retrieval metrics. Furthermore, in physical experiments conducted under a zero-shot transfer setting, STARE achieves an overall success rate of 80%. Our project page and code are provided in the Supplementary Materials.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 STARE 方法，面向服务机器人依据包含视觉特征与场景文字的自由指令检索日常物体，用 Crosslingual Visual Prompt 增强场景文字理解并建模指令实体与物体关系，并构建 GoGetIt、TextCaps-test 两个基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于机器人视觉语言检索任务，主要解决跨模态匹配与场景文字识别，未涉及 latent 推理状态、证据筛选、停止决策或训练监督机制，缺乏可供核查的 LVR 迁移线索。
